title: A missing multiplicity condition for double-permutation sequences
verdict: PASS — finite obstruction and separated-term lemma

initial.analysis: For n=2 reverse-toggle swaps A and C, fixes B, all transitions adjacent different-body, period cannot divide four. No mixed events; each internal tangent with opposite side labels gives one directed mixed event. Separated-start argument counts one inversion per unordered cross-body endpoint pair, exactly fills half period, and reverse-toggle preserves the multiplicity class, forcing the opposite directed occurrence on return. Check exact historical scope separately.

checks: Eight-term A,B,A,B,C,B,C,B obeys primitive period eight, each step swaps one adjacent different-body pair, and reverse-toggle exchanges A and C and fixes B. Checking the directed order after each step gives four supporting types twice, no mixed pair at any step. The original encoding demands the two internal tangents and both directions, hence mixed types. Changing phase, reversing traversal, and relabeling preserve the obstruction.

From a fully separated term D, every one of the 4 binomial(n,2) possible cross-body comparisons reverses by reverse-toggle. One adjacent swap reverses one comparison, filling exactly the available steps. The second half has one of each unordered type by reverse-toggle, with directed orientation opposite from returning to D. This does not give polygon construction.

limits: The literal dated-manuscript and workshop formulation only. Stronger multiplicity is prior work. No counterexample to valid-fibration theorem, no normalized-input polygon construction, no final Goodman–Pollack edition or historical-firstness claim.
